newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan to try 145 over bread price riots.
newsitem.headline: Jordan to try 145 over bread price riots.

text.p: Jordan will try 145 people for alleged involvement last month's riots that broke out after bread price rises, Information Minister Marwan Muasher said on Thursday.
Muasher told reporters that 107 of those facing charges had "participated in damaging public property".

He said the remaining 38 were members of political parties, mostly from the Jordanian Arab Socialist Baath Party (JASBP) which the government blames for helping stir up Jordan's worst civil disturbances in seven years.
The JASBP has denied involvement in the riots.
"We presented all the evidence to the courts," Muasher said. "We are convinced there was interference."
The two-day unrest began in the southern city of Karak on August 16 and spread to nearby towns before reaching a poor district in Amman.

Earlier this week a Jordanian official said 190 people had been detained in the unrest but Jordanian newspapers have quoted Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti as saying that 572 people had been arrested since the start of the disturbances.
There are still 51 people -- who are among those being put on trial -- in detention.
Kabariti said last month he had to raise bread prices to close a gaping budget deficit that threatened to undermine an IMF economic reform plan and the vital loans it would bring.
But the bread price hikes had a knock-on effect on at least 50 other food items, economists and traders said.

Bread is a staple for the poor majority of Jordan's 4.2 million population, facing falling standards of living, unemployment and still awaiting promised economic dividends from the controversial 1994 peace treaty with Israel.
